correctness.rationale: An interval-support argument exhaustively classifies all weight-one and weight-two upper-triangular matrices. The parity-check conditions are necessary and sufficient to exclude these; every projective direction supplies a unique nonzero weight-one syndrome, and a three-point diagonal dependence yields distance exactly three. The count multiplies freely choosable basis images and divides by the free postcomposition action of GL(alpha,q). The independent executable checks 11,346 explicitly classified low-weight cases and all 8,192 smallest binary low-band matrices.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full-text paper proves a numerical characterization conditional on minimum distance three and exhibits perfect codes at codimension three only; the 2023 full-text paper studies the rank-three maximum-distance construction. Neither inspected source supplies all-codimension existence, the unrestricted full-kernel classification, or the exact number of labeled perfect subspaces. The new local obstruction proof and orbit count establish these statements. A generalization of earlier geometric ingredients is properly credited; possible unindexed equivalence remains.
residual_risks: The generalized parity-check observation is close to the published rank-three construction; an unindexed equivalent all-codimension statement or enumeration could exist.
No classification under the full flag-rank isometry group is claimed.

value.rationale: The 2026 perfect-code paper gives the length equation only conditional on code existence and constructs one codimension. The new theorem resolves existence for every admissible codimension, classifies all such codes, and counts the entire labeled parameter family. This naturally completes the fundamental radius-one flag-rank perfect-code question rather than optimizing an arbitrary short instance; the result distinguishes the flag metric from ordinary Hamming syndromes through a necessary local-span restriction.
